title: Application-core feature streams exiting early
first_prompt:
This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.

<system-reminder>
<tools-used-before-summary>Ag

commits.summary: example-targets negative N0: the Spring CVE catalog, 285-300, with every revision checked upstream
commits.body:
Imports the archived research registry's 15 Spring CVEs and the seed file's CVE-2025-22234 as real-world examples 285-300, each with example.json, a target.json sidecar (example-target/v1) and a hand-written README. CVE-2023-34055 (285), CVE-2022-22968 (286) and CVE-2025-22228 (287) are promoted in place with role negative and no tasks yet (N1-N3 add them); the other 13 are catalog entries with no preparation, tasks or verdict, whose missing prerequisites are the registry's model blockers, recorded as predicted handoff blockers. 300 is research only, linked to 287, with its vendor-attributed introduction and no timing oracle.

Every revision was checked against upstream on github.com, so each sidecar says checked-upstream: the release tags resolved with git ls-remote; the 17 fix commits and their recorded parents fetched as commit objects (no trees); and each fix shown to be an ancestor of its fixed release and not of its vulnerable one with git merge-base, on a treeless fetch. Everything matched the registry. Release pairs and exact-fix pairs are kept separate, and no execution pair is selected yet. examples/tags.json gains 11 tags, added at the end of each facet and listed under its $negative key.

commits.summary: example-targets negative N1: the CVE-2023-34055 method-label packet (285), source-locked with frozen claims, oracle, carrier, driver and mutant
commits.body:
Example 285 (Spring Boot WebMvcTags.method, CVE-2023-34055) becomes a deep negative packet ready for Phase 5's preparation. The release pair 2.7.17 -> 2.7.18 is selected, on the published-artifact route: the exact-fix pair 7ad6e447 -> 5490e739 has no published JAR, and each release's WebMvcTags.java is that pair's blob (also in the sources JARs), with Tag, ImmutableTag and HttpMethod byte-identical across the two releases' closures. sources.lock.json records the blobs, the managed versions, each release's seven-JAR class path with sha256 (sha1 checked against Maven Central) and what javap shows of the method, its class initializer and its callees.

target.json has four tasks, all native strict and requiring the replay: replay (concrete controls on the pair); vulnerable-security (expected refuted) and fixed-security (expected established), sharing claims/bounded-method-label.json, whose label set is frozen as Spring Framework 5.3's eight HttpMethod names plus UNKNOWN; and preservation (expected established) of the eight names and the null request outside the allowed change. The claim files follow the workflow stream's example-target-claim/v1 (on its branch); they validate against its schema and its W1 planner plans all four tasks from this folder. The packet adds a request carrier that hands the raw token through unchanged and throws from every other servlet method, a minimal adapter and a JSON-lines driver (--release 21), 15 probes, an independent oracle whose self-test rejects an all-UNKNOWN implementation and refuses malformed or incomplete output, and a mutation patch that restores raw emission in the fixed release's fallback.

Verified: the integration script passes (contract 3 pass and 13 stubs, targets 41, test_build 190, test_pipeline 29, every sidecar valid through build.py --plan). As a developer note only, the pinned JARs were fetched by hand and run in separate JVMs on Temurin 21.0.13 and 25.0.5: 2.7.17 violates the property at exactly the five trigger probes, 2.7.18 holds, the mutant fails at the same five, every legitimate probe passes on all three, and the outputs are identical on both JDKs. No verifier ran; the blockers stay predicted. The stream brief's Progress records two interface requests for the merge: a constructed mutant as a revision, and how a driver is invoked.

commits.summary: example-targets negative N2: the CVE-2022-22968 binder packet (286), source-locked, with the decision lemma, preservation and protected-state claims, oracle, driver and mutant
commits.body:
Example 286 is now a deep negative packet. It selects the release pair (Spring Framework 5.3.18 -> 5.3.19, published JARs). Each release's DataBinder.java is the exact-fix pair's blob (612dfc56, 8ee5e43b), and the decision's helpers are byte-identical across the closures. Two CachedIntrospectionResults commits in the release window filter properties the probe bean doesn't have, and the driver prints the resolved properties on every run. sources.lock.json records the tags, commits, blobs, ancestry, the other commits between the releases, the JARs' sha1 against Maven Central with their sha256, and the javap facts.

There are three claims and six tasks. The decision lemma (vulnerable-security, expected refuted; fixed-security, expected established): a field that a canonical disallowed pattern matches ignoring ASCII case is denied. Preservation (established): outside the case aliases, both releases decide alike. The protected-state claim, on the actual bind (its own vulnerable and fixed tasks): with AGE or age disallowed, binding a simple name never writes age. The domain is ASCII, a canonical field, and the default locale pinned to Locale.ROOT. The claims validate against the workflow stream's W1 schema, and its plan_task plans all six tasks.

The controls: a delegating subclass that exposes the protected isAllowed, adapters that catch nothing, a driver, 46 probes, an independent oracle with a self-test, and a mutant that lower-cases one side only. The probes are 35 decisions and 11 bindings, five of their configurations copied from the upstream tests. Run by hand with pinned JARs on Temurin 21.0.13 and 25.0.5, a developer note and not evidence: 5.3.18 fails at exactly the 12 triggers and passes every legitimate probe; 5.3.19 holds; preservation holds; the mutant fails 13 probes and passes the legitimate ones. The output lines were identical on both JDKs. The integration script passes.

For review, under Progress. Outside the ASCII domain, 5.3.19 allows dataΣx against the pattern dataΣ*, which 5.3.18 denies by exact match: String.toLowerCase maps the final sigma by context, in any locale. Under tr-TR, 5.3.19 allows an alias (example 288's property).

Where the brief is out of date: N2 asks for the upstream 'changed wildcard and map tests', but a7cf19ce changes no wildcard test. bindingWithAllowedFieldsUsingAsterisks is only renamed. The packet copies that test's inputs and adds constructed disallowed wildcards, as recorded in target.json's unresolved list.

commits.summary: example-targets negative N3: the CVE-2025-22228 BCrypt packet (287), source-locked, with the public matches claim, preservation, a byte-array guard lemma, oracle, independent stored hashes, driver and mutant
commits.body:
Example 287 is now a deep negative packet ready for Phase 5's preparation. The release pair (Security 6.3.7 -> 6.3.8, published artifacts: spring-security-crypto, then each release's spring-jcl) is the execution pair. It carries the exact fix 36ea1b11 -> 46f0dc6d faithfully: both releases' BCrypt.java and BCryptPasswordEncoder.java are that pair's blobs, also in the sources JARs, and in the class files only BCrypt.hashpw(byte[], String, boolean) differs (compared method by method; sources.lock.json).

Three claims, frozen and valid against the workflow stream's example-target-claim/v1. The public claim is shared by vulnerable-security (expected refuted) and fixed-security (expected established): for a valid stored hash, BCryptPasswordEncoder.matches throws IllegalArgumentException exactly when the candidate is longer than 72 UTF-8 bytes (the JDK's count), and never returns true for one, with Strings bounded at 80 units so the rejected branch is reachable. Preservation (expected established) holds outside 'a non-null candidate longer than 72 UTF-8 bytes'. A narrower byte-array lemma on BCrypt.checkpw(byte[], String) has its own diagnostic tasks, each with its security task as parent. The workflow stream's plan_task plans all six tasks.

The controls: a one-call adapter; a driver that passes candidates as UTF-16 units and prints the JDK's byte count; 33 probes against 9 stored hashes made independently by pyca bcrypt from recorded preimages (never encode(overlong), which upstream's own test relies on); an oracle written from the statement, whose self-test rejects deny-all and reject-all implementations; and a mutant on 6.3.8 that counts UTF-16 units instead of bytes.

Verified: a hand run with the pinned JARs on Temurin 21 and 25 (a developer note, not evidence) gave exactly the outcomes written before the run. 6.3.7 authenticates 9 overlong candidates (ASCII, minors b and y, 36 x U+00E9 plus x, 18 supplementary characters plus x, a split character, byte arrays). 6.3.8 rejects all 12 overlong probes and keeps every legitimate match. The mutant authenticates the multibyte ones. A generated Java harness confirmed that the claim's own expressions agree with the oracle. The integration script passes (contract 3 and 13 stubs, targets 41, test_build 190, test_pipeline 29, every sidecar valid). No verifier job was queued: Phase 5 runs the capability probe on prepared artifacts. Four blockers are recorded as predicted, among them the precise cryptographic gap (no summary of crypt_raw is claimed).

For review, in the brief's Progress: lone surrogates match a hash of '?'s on every revision; a cost-31 hash never terminates (an int loop counter, read from the bytecode); 6.3.8 locks out legitimately stored long passwords (N4's ground); and the frozen claim is the strict rejection policy, stricter than the seed's 'may reject'. The rest of the brief is accurate.
